items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

ctx.x: was. Most — I’m a self-taught arranger. And I’m self-taught on the piano. I feel like a little kid. You know Dino Govoni who teaches, he’s a very good saxophone player across the hall from me at Berklee. I played piano once in his room, I was trying out the piano in his room. We all have pianos. And I played for about twenty minutes. He was smiling. He says, “Fred, when you play you’re like a little kid.” He said, and he loves me on saxophone, alto or tenor. He says, “If I could play piano like you I’d give up my…

Find your thing. So I play a certain — I’m looking at my students, my saxophone students, “How do you play like that.” I said, “I just kept playing over the years.” And I’m talking and I go [scats] you know four octaves down on some kind of pentatonic thing. If it’s in my fingers, in the last ten years, I got it. And with weird, crab-like fingerings. And I’m looking. I’m just being silly.
